positive.name: a pace decision with a 90-minute ttl, run with --dry-run so the hook prints the JSON it would write and writes nothing. --file names a throwaway path under fixtures/window-fit/ that does not exist, so no kept fields are read and the control never reads or writes ~/.dispatch/budget-decision.json, which the gate and the ledger guard treat as ground truth. Proves the clock-stamp path runs and the given fields land. No `touches` entry: nothing is written.

negative.name: a typed written_at stamp (observation 0343: a controller once typed a planned launch time into written_at). The hook must refuse with exit 2 before parsing anything else and print no budget JSON. Same --dry-run and throwaway --file as the positive control, so nothing is read from or written to ~/.dispatch even if the refusal regressed.
a ttl past the 5-hour ceiling (6h): the file must never outlive one 5-hour window, so the hook refuses with exit 2 and prints no budget JSON. Same --dry-run and throwaway --file as above.

turbo with --parallel none (owner 2026-10-20, observation 0470: the null ceiling read as no cap and ten units ran on an 8-core rig on 2026-10-19). The writer refuses with exit 2 and prints no budget JSON. --dry-run and the throwaway --file as above, so nothing is read from or written to ~/.dispatch even if the refusal regressed; --windows-file names a path that does not exist.

a turbo ttl of 3h: turbo renews at every 2-hour check, so its file lives at most 2h (the 2026-10-19 file was renewed by hand for 5h). The writer refuses with exit 2 at any clock time, before the Overnight rule is read, and prints no budget JSON. Same --dry-run and throwaway paths.

a stop band of 97 (the 2026-10-16 file carried 85/97, and launch_throttle read it raw, relaxing the 95 hard stop). The writer refuses any stop band outside 50-95 with exit 2 and prints no budget JSON. Same --dry-run and throwaway paths.
